maya: Heads-up — CI red on `timer_shutdown_order_test` in run 78 (linux/clang, shard 3). Looks timing/nondet. Logs attached below.

maya: ````
E tests/timer_test.cc:87: Assertion `events[i] == expected[i]' failed
Test: timer_shutdown_order_test
seed=4839201
Stack:
  at run_timers (eng/runtime/timer.cc:312)
  at TimerTest_ShutdownOrder (tests/timer_test.cc:45)
````

rahul: saw that too in the nightly matrix. Reproduces locally intermittently for me with repeated runs (~2/200).

owen: can you confirm the seed? CI log shows `seed=4839201` like you pasted.

maya: yep seed=4839201. Local repro I used: `bazel test //eng/runtime:timer_test --test_arg=--gtest_filter=timer_shutdown_order_test --test_arg=--seed=4839201 --runs_per_test=50` — reproduced 1/50 here.

ci-bot: Re-run requested by @rahul: job 78 -> rerun #2 queued, started, finished (status: failed). Rerun #3 queued.

rahul: ok, failing across reruns so not a one-off. Can someone bisect between `abc1234` and `def5678`? suspect recent scheduler micro-optimizations.

maya: I can start bisecting today. Quick note: test manipulates steady_clock and relies on relative ordering; might be sensitive to spurious wakeups.

sarah: short-term patch option: stub out the real clock for the test or add deterministic mock to force ordering. Long-term we should make the test tolerant to reordering (or assert on multiset equality).

owen: agree with @sarah — mocking is safest for immediate flake mitigation. If someone wants to add a small sleep in test as band-aid, ok but prefer mock.

maya: I'll sketch a mock-based fix and post a PR. Meanwhile I'll run a quick git bisect (starting now) and report the first bad commit.

rahul: ping me when you have the bisect range; I can do a faster bisect on CI if needed. Also FYI build 78 includes commit `c3f9b2a` (merge from scheduler-refactor).

ci-bot: Bisect job triggered by @maya: bisect-run-1 queued.

dave: if you need extended test runners / parallelization to speed bisect, ping infra (I can allocate).

maya: thanks — assigning myself to triage. Plan: (1) verify local bisect -> identify offending commit, (2) open quick PR with test mock if bisect shows behavior change, (3) follow-up with proper fix in scheduler code.

rahul: sounds good. keep thread updated. :eyes:

maya: quick update — bisect preliminary says first bad commit likely `c3f9b2a` (same as rahul noted). I'll push a draft PR for the mock now and link it here when ready. :thumbsup:

owen: nice — thanks for owning this.

ci-bot: Draft PR created: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/1423 (status: draft).

maya: will land a temp test fix on Monday if CI remains flaky, then follow up with scheduler change.

sarah: thanks. If anyone sees related flakes in other timer tests, reply here with seed and run id.

maya: closing this wave of investigation for now, will reopen if bisect changes. :wave:
